plain_text:
Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) affects the
brain's ability to focus and control impulses and is one of
the most common mental disorders that children experience.
It can also continue into adulthood.
semantic_text: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) affects the brain's ability to focus and control impulses and is one of the most common mental disorders that children experience. It can also continue into adulthood.

plain_text:
ADHD shows up first in childhood, sometimes as early as age 3.
It's not unusual for children to be energetic, act impulsively, and
have trouble focusing from time to time. But for children with
ADHD, these behaviors are persistent and can be disruptive to
both the child and those around them.
semantic_text: ADHD shows up first in childhood, sometimes as early as age 3. It's not unusual for children to be energetic, act impulsively, and have trouble focusing from time to time. But for children with ADHD, these behaviors are persistent and can be disruptive to both the child and those around them.

plain_text:
The most common symptoms of childhood ADHD are
hyperactivity, impulsivity, and inattention. These symptoms can
show up in different ways—for example, not all children with
ADHD appear hyperactive. ADHD may also look different in one
setting compared to another (such as at home versus at school).
semantic_text: The most common symptoms of childhood ADHD are hyperactivity, impulsivity, and inattention. These symptoms can show up in different ways—for example, not all children with ADHD appear hyperactive. ADHD may also look different in one setting compared to another (such as at home versus at school).

plain_text:
■ Have trouble paying attention to details, following directions,
or staying focused on tasks
■ Be easily distracted by their own thoughts or by things
happening around them
■ Seem fidgety or restless or struggle to engage in quiet
activities
■ Act impulsively—for example, by interrupting others often
■ Hyperfocus on activities that are interesting or meaningful
to them (often to the point of being unable to shift focus to
something else)

plain_text:
These symptoms can affect a child's relationships with their
families and with other children. They can also affect a child's
performance in school and their overall well-being.
semantic_text: These symptoms can affect a child's relationships with their families and with other children. They can also affect a child's performance in school and their overall well-being.

plain_text:
ADHD symptoms can first appear in children
as young as age 3 and continue into
adulthood. To be diagnosed with ADHD,
adolescents and adults must have
experienced symptoms before age 12.
semantic_text: ADHD symptoms can first appear in children as young as age 3 and continue into adulthood. To be diagnosed with ADHD, adolescents and adults must have experienced symptoms before age 12.

plain_text: SOURCE: NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF MENTAL HEALTH
semantic_text: SOURCE: NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF MENTAL HEALTH

plain_text:
As children with ADHD enter adolescence, their symptoms can
change. Pressure at school, relationships with peers, increasing
responsibilities, and hormonal changes can all influence ADHD in
new ways.
semantic_text: As children with ADHD enter adolescence, their symptoms can change. Pressure at school, relationships with peers, increasing responsibilities, and hormonal changes can all influence ADHD in new ways.

plain_text:
Challenges with paying attention, impulsivity, and executive
functioning in teenagers can result in:
semantic_text: Challenges with paying attention, impulsivity, and executive functioning in teenagers can result in:

plain_text:
■ Poor time management and organizational skills
■ Difficulty prioritizing tasks and completing assignments on time
■ Trouble managing emotions and dealing with frustration
■ Risky or impulsive behaviors (such as substance use or unprotected sex)
semantic_text: ■ Poor time management and organizational skills ■ Difficulty prioritizing tasks and completing assignments on time ■ Trouble managing emotions and dealing with frustration ■ Risky or impulsive behaviors (such as substance use or unprotected sex)

plain_text:
Like in childhood, ADHD can affect teenagers' social relationships,
self-esteem, and performance in school. Teenagers with ADHD
may also experience mental health issues such as depression
and anxiety.
semantic_text: Like in childhood, ADHD can affect teenagers' social relationships, self-esteem, and performance in school. Teenagers with ADHD may also experience mental health issues such as depression and anxiety.

plain_text: Learn more about ADHD in children and teens.
semantic_text: Learn more about ADHD in children and teens.

plain_text:
The right treatment, support, and coping strategies can help young
people with ADHD at each stage of their development.
semantic_text: The right treatment, support, and coping strategies can help young people with ADHD at each stage of their development.

plain_text:
Here are some ways parents, teachers, and other caregivers can
help young people navigate ADHD from childhood through
adolescence.
semantic_text: Here are some ways parents, teachers, and other caregivers can help young people navigate ADHD from childhood through adolescence.

plain_text:
■ Structure and routine. Children with ADHD thrive on
predictability. Set a consistent schedule and stick to it as much
as possible. This provides a sense of stability and helps them stay
on track.
■ Clear communication. Use clear, simple, direct language to
explain rules and expectations.
■ Coping strategies. Teach them skills for managing emotions,
staying organized, and reducing stress. Help them break
overwhelming tasks into smaller, more manageable steps.
